title: Koszul and quotient towers have the same limit
statement:
Let $X,\Lambda,I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ and $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]. Put $P_m=\Lambda/I^m$, and use $Q_m$ and its transitions from [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-koszul-completion]. For this assertion, both derived inverse limits are computed by the total right derived inverse-limit functor on strict towers of $\Lambda_X$-module complexes [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]; its product-cone triangle gives a choice of the adic derived inverse limit [def-weil-pbc-adic-derived-inverse-limit]. Compute the two towers with one K-flat representative of $K$ [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Define $\kappa_K$ and $\operatorname{comp}_K$ [def-weil-pbc-completion-map] using the strict compatible maps induced respectively by $\Lambda\to Q_m$ (the degree-zero inclusion) and $\Lambda\to P_m$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$c_K:K^{\wedge,\mathrm{Kos}}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_m K_m$$
induced by the strict quotient augmentations $Q_m\to P_m$, and it satisfies $c_K\circ\kappa_K=\operatorname{comp}_K$.

proof.text: Apply the strict tensor augmentation statement to obtain all v_n, their unit and zero-summand formulas and their strict transition squares.

The canonical map from the ring unit to the constant module sheaf on Λ is an isomorphism. Construct its inverse by the module sheafification adjunction applied to the section 1 of the restricted ring-unit module. To prove the two inverse equations, test maps from the unit on 1, and test maps from the sheafification using the adjunction and the same generator. The exterior degree-zero equivalence and the reindexing isomorphism then make koszulSheafUnitZero invertible. Naturality of the monoidal right unitor and whisker exchange prove naturality of the Koszul tensor unit. For any compatible g and σ, test the proposed levelwise naturality equation on every total tensor summand: nonzero Koszul degrees vanish on both sides; on degree zero cancel the invertible unitor followed by tensoring the Koszul unit, and use the assumed augmentation square. Thus naturality follows from the unit and zero-summand properties and is proved here, not left in the augmentation intermediate theorem.

For each model set V=product(v_n). Check (1-shift_Koszul) V=V (1-shift_quotient) by composing with every product projection and using the transition equation. Define w by the mapping-cocone lift with first coordinate fst composed with V and degree-minus-one coordinate snd composed with V. The differential identity δ(snd)=-ofHom(fst composed with (1-shift)) proves the lift equation. The mapping-cocone lift identities give both required coordinates.
Apply invertibility of the explicit quotient cone comparison to these v and w and use asIso(Q(w)) for c. Its hom is definitionally Q(w).

The Koszul completion unit has first coordinate product(koszulTensorUnit) and second coordinate zero. The levelwise unit formula therefore proves that its composite with w is the quotient completion chain map, by the two-coordinate extensionality of the mapping cocone. Localize this chain-map equality and precompose with the inverse of the model realization to get the required derived unit equation.

The levelwise naturality equation implies V_M product(σ)=product(τ) V_N by product extensionality. Compose w_M b and a w_N with both mapping-cocone coordinates. The assumed formulas for a and b and this product equation make both coordinates agree. The identity decomposition into the two mapping-cocone summands proves the chain maps equal. Localize this equality to get the final naturality equation.
